title: Every segmented control is Apple's own Liquid Glass segmented control
goal: You asked on 2026-09-29 why the app was not using the Mac's own Liquid Glass segmented control. Every row of side-by-side choices is now the system control itself, one continuous track in the title bar and in the panel. What is left is your yes: the Mac fills the picked choice with the accent colour and switches without a slide, which may not be the glass you pictured.
acceptance: Every segmented choice in the app (title bar View | Edit, the history bar filter, every panel picker; inventory in the task log) is the system's segmented control: SwiftUI Picker with .pickerStyle(.segmented) (or NSSegmentedControl with segmentStyle .rounded/.automatic as ONE capsule, trackingMode selectOne) so macOS 26 draws it with its own Liquid Glass and its own selection motion; our custom rail, glass pane, thumb motion, SegmentThumbMorph and the plate styles are deleted

In the title bar it is one continuous capsule with a sliding selection, not separated buttons: check its rendered style there, and if the titlebar accessory forces the separated look, host it so it renders as the standard control (photographed)

Sizes use the system control sizes (.small in dense panel rows and the title bar to sit with the panel toggle, .regular elsewhere); icons with tooltips where the options are icons; disabled options disabled by the system
Behaviour kept: a pick inside another animation does not disturb it, keyboard focus and arrows work, walks can press each segment by name and by pointer click
comp-segmented.html becomes a page that documents the system control (when to use it, sizes, do and don't) with a note of this decision, and UX-PATTERNS says the segmented control is the system's

The unreadable-label task (the-picked-segment-s-label-is-readable-on-the-gl) is dropped as superseded once this lands, since the system control owns its contrast; photographs of all placements in light and dark confirm the selected label is readable
A card shows the user photographs of each placement before/after and a short filmed move, asking them to confirm this is what they wanted

log.note: owns these walks: segmented-thumb-glass-walk, segmented-thumb-film-walk, segment-tooltips-walk, transition-placement-and-hold-walk, transition-edge-follows-the-pointer-walk

Inventory: 34 segmented controls in 23 files, all through SegmentedControl: title bar View|Edit, history filter, Library scope, Text Across/Down, Captions align, Arrowhead ending, path line pattern/end/corner, Arrangement (3), Measure (3+3), Callout (2), Canvas, Grid settings, Colour picker (2), Transition overlap, Property keys path shape, Caption lines, Tool settings capsule, Resize, Export/Video/Recording export dialogs (9), Recording setup. No caller used a per-option disabled state.

Adversarial review before building: SwiftUI Picker(.segmented) cannot do it (measured: never stretches, a 280pt frame stays 87pt; and it resets NSSegmentedControl.segmentStyle to .automatic on every update). So SegmentedControl wraps NSSegmentedControl directly: .rounded pinned, .selectOne, fill form equal columns or proportional, ViewThatFits to a dropdown when words cannot fit, per-option selectionDisabled via setEnabled(forSegment:), tooltips via the app's HintAnchors laid over equal segments, picture options now NSImage (their accessibilityDescription is the name a walk presses). The Next switch next-designed-segmented stays so Current keeps its SwiftUI picker.

What macOS 26 draws, measured in the probe (styles automatic, rounded and capsule compared in panel, title bar and history bar; front and back): all three styles look identical; one continuous track in the title bar (the reported separated look was NOT reproduced, with automatic either); picked segment accent blue when the window is in front, grey behind; Cmd-2 switches with no slide (filmed densely). Pointer-click film has no frames while the click is held, so a slide there cannot be ruled out. No glass selection pane.

Deleted: DesignedSegments, thumb/glass/rail palette, SegmentColumnsLayout, SegmentThumbDrag (PhotonzCore) + tests, Scripts/segmented-gallery.swift + its test.sh typecheck. SegmentedControlUsageTests now asserts the system control (NSSegmentedControl(), .rounded, .selectOne) and fails on glassEffect/thumb words. Video panel rows (Transition overlap, Property keys, Caption lines, Library scope) now ask for .small like every other panel row: at regular size 'Before the cut | Across it | After it' collapsed to its dropdown.

Verified: Scripts/test.sh 10560/10560. Walks: segmented-thumb-glass-walk (rewritten: the thumb drag became pointer presses; title bar pressed by pointer both ways) and segmented-thumb-film-walk (title bar films kept, panel films became pointer presses) green; 10 walks that read 'already on' + 108 caption/export/library/measure/callout/arrow/transition/colour/view-mode walks: all green after the .small fix (two transition walks had failed on the collapsed row). Front-of-screen copies of both walks run while the user was away for the active-look pictures.

Docs: comp-segmented.html rewritten to document the system control (it is what this task asked); UX-PATTERNS 'The one segmented control' says the control is the system's. Audit queue/audits/2026-09-29-system-segmented.json. Card asks the user to confirm (keep / glass toolbar for View|Edit / back to drawn). Readable-label task was already dropped; the-segmented-thumb-moves-the-way-the-user-likes dropped and its card withdrawn as superseded.

left rough (not filed, in the audit): segment tooltips are laid over equal columns, so a .fill row squeezed to proportional widths would place a tooltip slightly off (no such row has tooltips today); mock set's shared segmented.css still draws the old rail on other mock pages (mocks are never edited to match code).

Built and verified: every segmented control in Next is the Mac's own NSSegmentedControl, one continuous track (tests 10560/10560, 118 segment walks green, audit 2026-09-29-system-segmented). Waiting on the user's confirmation card: macOS 26 fills the pick with the accent colour in front and switches without sliding, which may not be the glass they pictured.

folded in from a-walk-can-click-the-history-bar-and-film-its-fi (dropped 2026-09-30 by triage): a scripted walk still cannot press anything in the history bar (the bar never becomes the key window during a walk), so the history filter's clicks are proven only by it being the same system control the title bar and panel walks press. If the user reports the history filter not answering a click, this is where to start: PlaytestHarness.panelWindows() does not look in the history panel.
